description: Every table carrying a tenant_id column, its database isolation model, and its cross-tenant adversarial-proof status. tenant:isolation:check fails if a tenant-scoped table exists in the migrations but is absent here, or a registered table no longer exists — so a new tenant-owned table cannot ship unnoticed.

proofStates.pending: tenant_id enforced at the schema level, but no cross-tenant negative test proves A cannot reach B.
proofStates.proven: a negative test named in testReference proves cross-tenant read/write is rejected.

tables.isolationNote: Schema is correctly tenant-scoped, but recordRiskDecision() and every sibling authority pin tenantId = PLATFORM.DEFAULT_TENANT_ID (RiskDecisionInput carries no tenant). No caller supplies a second tenant, so cross-tenant behaviour is unexercised and cannot be proven through the real authority yet. Promotion is blocked on wiring a per-request tenant into the risk domain, not on writing a test.

tables.isolationNote: The tenant_id column is dormant: the INSERT never sets it (it relies on the DEFAULT), the UNIQUE key is (withdrawal_id, generation) with no tenant_id, every read/update filters WHERE withdrawal_id/id, and the parent withdrawals table has no tenant_id column at all (only user_id). The whole withdrawal domain is effectively single-tenant today. A cross-tenant negative test cannot be written without fabricating multi-tenant behaviour the code does not implement. #109 for this domain first requires adding tenant_id to withdrawals and threading a real tenant through the external-effect authority.
